subject: Mathematics

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.title is 'When the child rushes a station and skips counting/checking — repairing the no-check trap at Grade 3' and recovery_moves = ['Pencil-touch each.', 'Drill count out loud.', 'Compare guess vs count.'] — the 'no-check trap' is generic procedural advice, not a research-grounded G3 spatial-reasoning misconception, and recovery moves are terse with no diagnostic branching.
category_feedback.required_fix: Replace the no-check trap with a real G3 spatial-reasoning misconception cited to research (e.g., Battista's levels of geometric thinking — child names solids by holistic appearance rather than by counting faces/edges/vertices, treating a square pyramid and a triangular prism as 'the same' because both 'have triangles'). Provide branching recovery: if child can name attributes verbally but miscounts, scaffold pencil-touch counting; if child names by silhouette only, drop back to face-by-face tracing on a paper net before recounting on the solid.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: lesson_specific_materials lists 'Big Map Templates (1 per child)' and 'All previous manipulatives at 4 stations' as required, and differentiation.for_movement_learners = 'Walk between 4 stations physically.' — there is no explicit NO-PAPER, NO-PURCHASE alternative path for a day when prep wasn't possible.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a no-materials capstone alternative to differentiation, e.g., 'No-prep version — children rotate to 4 corners of the carpet. Corner 1: hold up fingers for faces of teacher-named solid. Corner 2: body-build a 3-part structure with partner (one squats=cube, one stands=prism, one points up=pyramid). Corner 3: clap-match congruent shapes teacher draws in the air. Corner 4: walk a 4-step route teacher calls aloud with quarter/half body turns. No paper required.'

category_feedback.specific_evidence: consolidation.exit_routine = 'Each child shares ONE: Today I learned ___.' and discussion_prompts are plain Q&A — there is no distinctive Tig-and-Coco quotable refrain or memorable chant carried across the unit's capstone.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a recurring refrain children chant back at consolidation, e.g., 'Trekker Tig and Compass Coco close every case: SORT, BUILD, MATCH, MOVE — that's how geometers GROOVE!' with a 4-beat hand-tap pattern (one tap per word: sort/build/match/move). Embed the same refrain in the minds_on hook so it bookends the lesson.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: action.steps and expanded_walkthrough have children execute the 4 station tasks and check by counting, but no step invites children to INVENT or COMPARE strategies, and the misconception is named only as 'no-check' — not in research-grounded terms (e.g., Battista's van Hiele Level 1 visual-holistic reasoning, or Clements & Sarama on G3 mental rotation).
category_feedback.required_fix: At Station 2 (BUILD) or Station 3 (MATCH), add a strategy-comparison move: 'Two geometers used different ways to check congruence — Tig overlapped the faces, Coco counted edge lengths. Which way works for YOUR pair? Try both and tell your partner which is faster and which is surer.' In expanded_walkthrough.rationale, name the misconception as Battista/van Hiele Level 1 (visual-holistic): G3 children often judge solids by overall silhouette rather than by analyzing faces/edges/vertices.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Lesson has 4 success_criteria mapped to 4 stations (SORT, COMPOSE, MATCH, FOLLOW), but worksheet has only 3 parts: Part 2 collapses COMPOSE and MATCH into a single decompose-and-match task. The worksheet does not deliberately VARY the practice format from the lesson nor justify the collapse as a transfer/generalization task.
category_feedback.required_fix: Either (a) split worksheet Part 2 into Part 2 (decompose 1 structure into 3 parts) and Part 3 (find 1 congruent face pair from a NEW set of 2 unfamiliar solids the lesson didn't drill, making the worksheet a transfer task), renumbering the map task to Part 4 — and add a teacher_notes line justifying the new pair as a generalization check; or (b) keep 3 parts but add 1 transfer item per part using solids/structures NOT seen at the matching station, and document the transfer rationale in worksheet teacher_notes.

grader_notes: Strong capstone scaffolding overall, but the 'no-check' trap reads as procedural rather than a real G3 spatial-reasoning misconception, the lesson lacks an explicit no-prep path, the consolidation has no quotable Tig/Coco refrain to anchor the unit's close, no strategy-comparison move appears, and the worksheet collapses 4 lesson stations into 3 parts without justifying it as transfer. Five 3s against the strict bar (≤1 score=3) — needs revision across both lesson and worksheet.
